claim: A Duke MASTERSWITCH, once operated, counts its hitag down by one each game tic (30 a second) and at zero operates its sector and arms its effectors: hitag 80 is a delay of about 2.67 seconds, not 8.
evidence: reference/eduke32/source/duke3d/src/actors.cpp:2554-2560 (G_MoveStandables; yvel == 1: --hitag <= 0, then G_OperateSectors and the effectors); duke3d.h:90 REALGAMETICSPERSEC 30
E4L1 sprite 119 (picnum 8, hitag 80) delays the briefing recorder's charges (projects/duke-e4l1-remake/briefing.py:54)
use: Convert a MASTERSWITCH delay as hitag/30 seconds, rounded to Blood's tenths.

checked.how: Read reference/eduke32/source/duke3d/src/actors.cpp:2554-2560 in G_MoveStandables (from :1916): MASTERSWITCH with yvel == 1 does --hitag <= 0, then G_OperateSectors and sets t_data[0] on SE 2/21/31/32/36 effectors; duke3d.h:90 REALGAMETICSPERSEC 30, so 80 is 2.67 s. Read maps/duke3d/E4L1.MAP sprite 119: picnum 8 (MASTERSWITCH), hitag 80, lotag 8000, sector 390. projects/duke-e4l1-remake/briefing.py:54 and inspect_briefing.py:60 use it.
